description: Composite three-panel figure: calculated stacking-fault-energy (SFE) maps of Fe–Mn–Al–C steels at room temperature drawn as 3-D surfaces; the group mixes two property surfaces (a, b) with a composition field/mechanism map (c). (a) SFE (mJ/m², 0–100, ticks every 20) versus C (wt%, 0–1.2, ticks 0.2) and Mn (wt%, 10–50, ticks 10); four stacked surfaces are labelled 3 wt.% Al, 5 wt.% Al, 8 wt.% Al and 11 wt.% Al, with SFE rising as C and Al increase. (b) SFE (same 0–100 axis) versus Al (wt%, 2–12, ticks 2) and Mn (wt%, 10–50) with six surfaces labelled 0 wt.% C, 0.3 wt.% C, 0.6 wt.% C, 0.9 wt.% C, 1.2 wt.% C and 1.5 wt.% C; SFE collapses toward low Al and rises with C. (c) 3-D composition map with C (wt%, 0–1.2) vertical and Al (2–12 wt%) and Mn (10–35 wt%) horizontal, partitioned into deformation-mechanism fields labelled TRIP, TWIP, MBIP, MBIP + Kappa and TWIP+Kappa, delimited by contours "Iso-SFE 20 mJ/m²", "Iso-SFE 50 mJ/m²" and a "Kappa-carbide forming border". Together the panels argue that Al, C (and Mn) raise SFE and thereby shift the mechanism TRIP→TWIP→MBIP with κ-carbide.

subfigures.description: 3-D surface plot of SFE (mJ/m², 0–100) against C (wt%, 0–1.2) and Mn (wt%, 10–50), with four colour-shaded surfaces labelled 3 wt.% Al, 5 wt.% Al, 8 wt.% Al and 11 wt.% Al stacked in order of increasing SFE; the steepest fall of SFE occurs toward C = 0.

3-D surface plot of SFE (mJ/m², 0–100) against Al (wt%, 2–12) and Mn (wt%, 10–50) with six surfaces labelled 0 wt.% C, 0.3 wt.% C, 0.6 wt.% C, 0.9 wt.% C, 1.2 wt.% C and 1.5 wt.% C; SFE increases with C and drops sharply as Al decreases toward 2 wt.%.

3-D composition map with C (wt%, 0–1.2) as the vertical axis and Al (wt%, 2–12) and Mn (wt%, 10–35) horizontal, coloured by SFE and divided into regions labelled TRIP, TWIP, MBIP, MBIP + Kappa and TWIP+Kappa, separated by 'Iso-SFE 20 mJ/m²', 'Iso-SFE 50 mJ/m²' and the 'Kappa-carbide forming border'.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a 3-D surface plot with SFE in mJ/m² on a 0–100 axis, C in wt% from 0 to 1.2 on one horizontal axis and Mn in wt% from 10 to 50 on the other.
Four SFE surfaces are labelled in panel (a): 3 wt.% Al, 5 wt.% Al, 8 wt.% Al and 11 wt.% Al, stacked with the 11 wt.% Al surface highest.
In panel (a) all surfaces fall toward the C = 0 edge, and the 11 wt.% Al surface approaches the top of the 100 mJ/m² axis while the 3 wt.% Al surface descends to the bottom of the plotted range.
Panel (b) plots SFE (0–100 mJ/m²) against Al (2–12 wt%) and Mn (10–50 wt%), with six surfaces labelled 0 wt.% C, 0.3 wt.% C, 0.6 wt.% C, 0.9 wt.% C, 1.2 wt.% C and 1.5 wt.% C.
In panel (b) SFE decreases steeply as Al decreases toward 2 wt.% for every C level, and higher C shifts the whole surface upward.
Panel (c) has axes C (wt%, 0–1.2), Al (wt%, 2–12) and Mn (wt%, 10–35) and is covered by a fine mesh surface coloured by SFE.
Panel (c) labels five deformation-mechanism regions: MBIP, MBIP + Kappa, TWIP, TWIP+Kappa and TRIP.
Panel (c) shows two iso-SFE boundaries labelled 'Iso-SFE 20 mJ/m²' and 'Iso-SFE 50 mJ/m²', plus a 'Kappa-carbide forming border'.

The caption states that (a) is SFE vs. C and Mn at different levels of Al, (b) is SFE vs. Al and Mn at different levels of C, and (c) is SFE vs. deformation mechanisms, for Fe–Mn–Al–C steels at room temperature.
The citing text states that Al and C linearly increase the SFE of austenite by 10 mJ/m² per wt% Al and 40 mJ/m² per wt% C, respectively, and that both suppress mechanical twinning.
The citing text states that Mn decreases the SFE between 0 and 15–20 wt% and increases it by 1.2–3 mJ/m² per wt% Mn at higher Mn contents.

The citing text states that the deformation mechanism of austenitic Fe-Mn-Al-C steels shifts from TRIP to TWIP and further to MBIP and MBIP together with κ-carbide precipitates as Al content (and hence SFE) increases, as predicted from the SFE maps of Fig. 24c.

The citing text additionally states that Si lowers SFE by 2.4–2.8 mJ/m²/wt% (with other sources reporting a non-monotonic dependence), that Cr lowers SFE, and that SFE decreases with increasing austenitic grain size; none of these variables is displayed in the panels.

unreadable_items: No numeric SFE value is printed on any surface of (a) or (b); the values can be read only against the 0–100 mJ/m² axis
Panel (c): no colour-bar/legend giving the numeric scale of the surface shading
Panel (c): mesh rendering is low resolution, so the exact shapes of the Iso-SFE 20 and 50 mJ/m² boundaries cannot be traced precisely
Panel (a)/(b): colour scale of the individual surfaces is not defined by a legend
